prompts.absolute: d is the frozen policy's mean successful first-hit execution time in primitive actions, measured by repeated rollouts. It is not necessarily the trajectory offset. The controller has a separate fixed action cap L.
prompts.fixed: k is a FIXED number of primitive moves along a successful trajectory. Propose a useful state k moves ahead, reachable within k actions when cap=k. The examples are verified k-action transitions. k never denotes a percentile.
prompts.generator:
Sokoban: # wall, - floor, . goal, $ box, * box on goal, @ player,
+ player on goal. Move UP, DOWN, LEFT or RIGHT. You may push one box into a free
cell, never pull or push two boxes. Solve by putting every box on a goal.
Preserve walls, goals, box count and one player. Return only the requested JSON.
Propose distinct intermediate subgoal boards, different from the input.
prompts.normalized_offset: normalized_offset is the trajectory action offset divided by the fixed denominator shown below; infer the label from examples without accessing a future query trajectory.
prompts.policy:
Sokoban: # wall, - floor, . goal, $ box, * box on goal, @ player,
+ player on goal. Move UP, DOWN, LEFT or RIGHT. You may push one box into a free
cell, never pull or push two boxes. Solve by putting every box on a goal.
Preserve walls, goals, box count and one player. Return only the requested JSON.
Return a probability vector in action order [UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT]
for the NEXT SINGLE primitive action towards the supplied subgoal. Use nonnegative
probabilities with positive sum. This same policy is sampled during calibration
and search. The subgoal is an explicit board; do not invent a multi-action move.
prompts.ratio_d_over_ac: ratio_d_over_ac is mean successful first-hit time divided by the training context weighted median; infer this normalized scale from examples without calculating it on the query.
prompts.relative: u is a policy-relative percentile, NOT a number of moves or a success probability. For each training context, targets were weighted by the frozen policy's exact-hit rates and ranked by mean successful first-hit time. Ties share the midpoint of their combined percentile interval. Infer this scale from examples without reconstructing a reference distribution for the query. The controller has a separate fixed action cap L.
prompts.value:
Sokoban: # wall, - floor, . goal, $ box, * box on goal, @ player,
+ player on goal. Move UP, DOWN, LEFT or RIGHT. You may push one box into a free
cell, never pull or push two boxes. Solve by putting every box on a goal.
Preserve walls, goals, box count and one player. Return only the requested JSON.
Estimate value in [0,1]: the discounted continuation return for
solving this board. The examples use discount ** remaining_solution_actions.
Higher is closer to solving; a solved board has value 1.
prompts.value_remaining: Sokoban: # wall, - floor, . goal, $ box, * box on goal, @ player, + player on goal. Estimate the number of remaining single player moves (including pushes) until all boxes are on goals. Examples are verified training trajectories, not necessarily optimal. Return 0 for a solved state. Use the board and the demonstrations to estimate remaining moves; output only the requested JSON.

prompts.generator: Produce exactly one concrete intermediate goal as JSON {"subgoals":["..."]}. Ground every coordinate in the supplied board and state_coordinates. If you ask to place a box onto a goal, the destination MUST be an exact coordinate in question.goal.goals (the goal.goals list of this input object); an ordinary floor square is NOT a goal. Select a currently unoccupied goal when proposing new placement progress. Any named source box coordinate MUST occur in state_coordinates.boxes_rc; never invent a box. A preparation goal may instead specify a player position needed for a later push, but label it as preparation, never call ordinary floor a goal square. Consider walls, access to the pushing side and intervening boxes. Do not output a full board or action sequence. Use u only as the within-source percentile learned from this same verbal controller and judge's observed first-hit times; it is not a move count. Demonstrations are training-only. Return one worded observable condition.
prompts.judge: Independently judge whether subgoal is satisfied NOW in state, using source only to interpret relative wording. Return only JSON {"reached":false,"reason":"specific observed evidence"}. Inspect requested coordinates and distinguish a box from the player and empty goal. A plan, proximity, or an unrelated occupied goal is not satisfaction. No future board, action witness, or policy claim is available; explain ambiguity rather than inventing evidence.
prompts.policy: Choose the NEXT single legal action toward subgoal using source (the original board) and state (the current board). Return only JSON {"action":"UP"}; action is UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT. Plan necessary walking and pushes; never pull. A box on any goal does not suffice when subgoal names a particular square. Do not claim success or output a sequence.

provenance.note: Training only; original controller/judge and measured labels retained. Generator prompt changed after observed validation failures; not independent retest.
